title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 24
paragraphs: When the cavalry reached the camp, the whole army and Mardonius himself made great mourning for Masistios — cutting off their own hair, their horses' and beasts of burden's, and giving themselves over to unrestrained lamentation. All Boeotia was filled with the sound of it, because the man who had perished was, after Mardonius, of the greatest account with the Persians and the king.
